title: Leaving Lunceford over too many one-nighters; manager Harold Oxley
summary: He left because of the one-nighters, said manager Oxley booked many, and notes the band's hits and many college dates.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Yeah, well, she was with Barnet back there then. In fact, when I left Lunceford I went with Barnet for a while. I left Lunceford because he did too many one nighters. You know, it was really -- it would kill you almost, you know.
Who was (inaudible)? Who was managing it?
The manager was Harold Oxley. But I don't know who was really booking the band, but I know he had -- he was the manager of the band, and we did an awful lot of onenighters.
You played all over the country, didn't you?

We did. The band was -- no, we didn't miss anything. The band was very popular because of their recordings. You know, Lunceford, at one time he must have had about seven, eight hits going at one time. And we did a lot of colleges. He was very -- this was back before colleges were really using name attractions, you know.

I don't imagine it was as lucrative as it is today playing colleges, but we played an awful lot of colleges. Of course, naturally, they were one nighters, you know. But Lunceford was a good businessman. He's -- I thought -- it was well organized, you know.
What kind of a person was he?
